parts.text: A student is investigating the reflection of light by a plane mirror. Her ray-trace sheet is shown in Fig. 3.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Measure and record in Table 3.1 the angle α between AN and CN, as shown in Fig. 3.1. [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Draw a normal to AB at point N , towards the top of the page. Label the top point of this normal L . [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Two pins P 1 and P 2 are placed on line LN, a suitable distance apart for ray tracing. On Fig. 3.1, label suitable positions for P 1 and P 2 . [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student places the reflecting surface of a plane mirror on line CD and views the images of P 1 and P 2 from the direction indicated by the eye in Fig. 3.1. She places two pins P 3 and P 4 so that the images of P 1 and P 2 , and the pins P 3 and P 4 , all appear exactly one behind the other.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Draw a line passing through P 3 and P 4 and reaching point N . [1]

ms.label: 3(b)(i)
ms.text: line in correct place and neat

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Measure the angle θ between this line and the normal LN . Record this value in Table 3.1. [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student moves the mirror to a line EF at an angle α = 35° to AN . Line EF is not shown in Fig. 3.1. The student repeats the process with the mirror on EF and places pins P 5 and P 6 in line with the new images.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Draw a line passing through P 5 and P 6 and reaching point N . [1]

ms.label: 3(c)(i)

parts.label: ii
